issues.target: B5 and A19: 'internally inconsistent' funding picture
issues.explanation: B5 calls the funding statements internally inconsistent, but the Form C ties them together. It says the issuer has resources for its near-term plan and is raising money to broaden participation, strengthen the balance sheet and add working-capital flexibility. It separately says the proceeds are 'essential'. That is a difference in wording and a tension, not a proven contradiction. B5's own note says it may be a framing difference. The 24-36 month runway cannot be checked because no monthly net-loss history is shown. The only reviewed loss figure covers about 2.7 months. Describe it as an unreconciled tension, not an inconsistency.

issues.target: A9 and B economics: 'zero debt' versus lender references
issues.explanation: The Form C reports zero debt and zero other securities. The Subscription Agreement refers to the Company's 'loan agreements' and 'existing credit facilities'. The risk factor on transfers says consent may be needed from 'potentially one or more lenders'. The use of proceeds lists 'debt service' as a possible use. Stage A noted only one of these references. They may be boilerplate, but they are three separate indications that conflict with the stated zero debt. The pack does not resolve this. Do not treat the zero-debt statement as settled.

issues.target: Capitalization: Form C ownership table versus April 30 note
issues.explanation: The Form C table gives TraderSumo 1,700,000 Units, which is 17% of 10,000,000 fully diluted. The April 30 note gives TraderSumo 15.0%. If Oasis (3,000,000) and Natural Workflow (1,500,000) are right, the implied Bethlem Royal holding is 300,000 Units (3%), against 5.0% in the note. The dates differ: April 30 is before the June 18 Unit denomination. Even so, the pack gives no reconciliation. Per-holder percentages should not be relied on until reconciled.

issues.target: A30 and A12: related-party payable versus zero liabilities
issues.explanation: Note 6 describes $10,000 of 'expenses payable' to Bethlem Royal, with $5,000 dated May 4, 2026. That date is after the April 30 balance sheet date. The balance sheet shows no liabilities, and the subsequent-events note says none. Either the amount was not a period-end liability, or the note and the balance sheet disagree. This is a question for the accountants and issuer, not a finding of misstatement.

issues.target: B8: founders' units 'even if the member stops providing services'
issues.explanation: B8 overstates the vesting terms. The Form C says a Vesting Member's Units are forfeited if it, or its principal service provider, voluntarily departs or is terminated for Cause before a Liquidity Event. The Units are retained on death, disability, removal without Cause or constructive termination. The 'no time-based retention' point is documented. The statement that Units are kept whenever service ends is not. Also, 'Liquidity Event' is undefined in the readable pages, so B8's incentive-alignment conclusion is speculative.

issues.target: A26 and B6: unlimited issuance without member consent
issues.explanation: Page 24 says there is no limit on Units that may be issued. The same Form C says securities issuances in excess of authorized amounts are a Reserved Matter needing approval of all three Managers. The Operating Agreement lets the Manager Committee update Exhibit A (the authorized and reserved Units) without Member consent. So no member consent is needed, but unanimous Manager approval is required above the 10,000,000 authorized Units. B6's 'open-ended dilution' omits this qualification. Dilution risk is real, since Managers control it, but the sources conflict on how it is capped.

issues.target: A20: 5% Pre-Distribution Cash allocation cannot be sized
issues.explanation: The pack text does not define 'Pre-Distribution Cash', so the effect of the 5% allocation on investors cannot be quantified. The Manager Committee also has discretion to retain or release unpaid amounts. The April 30 note calls the same mechanism the 'Funded Trader Profit Share Pool', while the Operating Agreement calls it the 'TradeFunded Capital Funding Allocation'. The definition and the recipient's related-party relationship need clarification.

issues.target: A21 and A29: distribution discretion versus tax distributions
issues.explanation: The Form C describes distributions as at the Manager Committee's absolute and sole discretion. Section 10.4 of the Operating Agreement says the Manager Committee 'shall cause' tax distributions 'to the extent practicable'. That provision assumes pass-through taxation. The Form C says that after the July 2 election the company is taxed as a corporation, with 1099-DIV reporting and no K-1. Whether Section 10.4 applies to offering investors is unclear and is not reconciled in the readable pages. A21 is not wrong. It omits this qualification.

issues.target: A16: Form C XML financial fields
issues.explanation: The XML shows cash of 0.00 and net income of 0.00 for the most recent fiscal year, with total assets of 226,885. It shows net income of -23115 in the prior-year field. This pattern fits a column or period placement error: the figures match the April 30 reviewed statements. That is an inference, not proven. Stage A marked financial_statements as 'contradictory'. That is defensible for the XML. The reviewed statements are internally consistent with the cover table. Do not treat the XML cash field as evidence of zero cash.

issues.target: Critical item statuses: operative_contract and closing_or_availability
issues.explanation: Operative_contract is marked 'confirmed_with_citation'. The pack lists it as present_unreviewed. Many Operating Agreement pages (Article IV-VIII, Liquidity Event, vesting, voting and Reserved Matters) were not processed. A better status is partially readable. The closing/availability item is 'not_found_in_pack' in Stage A, while the pack records availability as unknown because the platform was unreachable. That is a verification gap, not proof of non-availability or non-disclosure.

Stage A says the table is garbled and cites none of its figures. The key rows are readable: intermediary fees are $15,000 at the target and $34,800 at the maximum. Working capital and liquidity reserve is 44.882% ($305,199.98) at the maximum. The statement that trading accounts are 'funded solely from operating revenue' is forward-looking, so revenue of $0 up to April 30 does not by itself contradict it. It does raise a question about where trading capital would come from. The table also excludes some offering costs that are due before closing.

Stage A says no investor-side fees appear in the readable pages. The BitGo ACH terms in the pack (page 135) include a fee of up to $25 per returned transaction. Whether those terms apply to this offering is not established. The custody fee schedule is not in the readable pages. Investor-side custody and transaction fees remain unconfirmed.

issues.target: B2/K1-K3: implied equity values and PC2
issues.explanation: K1-K3 apply $0.35 to every issued Unit. The pack shows the Seed Investors' $250,000 over 1,000,000 Units is $0.25 per Unit, if all of it was paid by those investors. It also shows certain Founding Members received Units for no cash. So the 'implied equity value' is arithmetic on an arbitrary price and is not a measure of capital invested or of value. B2 states this, but the earlier-entry price is not mentioned. The arbitrary-price disclosure alone does not show overvaluation. No comparables or traction in the pack allow a test.

The team pages are not processed. The only documented history is the CTO's CFTC consent order, as described by the issuer. The full 'CFTC Action and Consent Order' section was not read. An adverse regulatory fact is relevant but is not a full execution record. Do not form a team conclusion from this one fact. The 0-employee figure is a Form C field. It does not show who performs the work, since contractors and affiliates are possible.

A32 states several provisions (deadline extension, intermediate closings) but cites only the cancellation and refund sentence. Extension and intermediate closings are in the pack on pages 9 and 23, with a 70% draw at the initial closing. A31 names BitGo and a trust arrangement, but its quote covers only the beneficial-ownership sentence. Page 8 supports the custodian and nominee. Add these citations. Also add the investor protections omitted from the rights analysis (C12), such as no additional capital calls.
